req.title: Deleting all tasks leaves empty table
req.statement: The system shall leave GET /tasks/ returning [] after every task has been deleted.
triggers: deleting all tasks leaves empty table

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-035 requires that after deleting every task, GET /tasks/ returns an empty list []. We need: (1) a positive test that creates multiple tasks, deletes each one, and asserts GET /tasks/ == []; (2) a negative test that attempts to delete a non-existent task and asserts HTTP 404; (3) a boundary test that creates exactly one task, deletes it, and asserts the list is empty (boundary of N=1). Additional tests cover state transitions and the exact 204 status code on successful delete. Each test uses an in-memory SQLite DB via dependency override to ensure isolation.

tests.name: test_delete_all_tasks_leaves_empty_list
preconditions: Multiple tasks are created via POST /tasks/
trace: R-TASK-035: system shall return [] after every task deleted
tests.executable:
import sqlalchemy, app.database as _db
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app import models
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

_engine = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
_Session = sessionmaker(bind=_engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=_engine)

def _override_get_db():
    db = _Session()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[_db.get_db] = _override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_all_tasks_leaves_empty_list():
    titles = ["Task A", "Task B", "Task C"]
    ids = []
    for t in titles:
        r = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": t, "completed": False})
        assert r.status_code == 201
        ids.append(r.json()["id"])
    assert len(ids) == 3
    for task_id in ids:
        r = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
        assert r.status_code == 204
    r = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json() == []

test_delete_all_tasks_leaves_empty_list()
app.dependency_overrides.clear()

import sqlalchemy, app.database as _db
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app import models
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

_engine = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
_Session = sessionmaker(bind=_engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=_engine)

def _override_get_db():
    db = _Session()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[_db.get_db] = _override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

def test_partial_delete_does_not_empty_list():
    r1 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "First", "completed": False})
    assert r1.status_code == 201
    id1 = r1.json()["id"]
    r2 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Second", "completed": False})
    assert r2.status_code == 201
    id2 = r2.json()["id"]
    r_del = client.delete(f"/tasks/{id1}")
    assert r_del.status_code == 204
    r_list = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert r_list.status_code == 200
    tasks = r_list.json()
    assert len(tasks) == 1
    assert tasks[0]["id"] == id2
    assert tasks[0]["title"] == "Second"

test_partial_delete_does_not_empty_list()
app.dependency_overrides.clear()
